questions.q: Why does Priya present Lesson 15's comparison matrix before touching any single case study in detail?
options: Because the panel requires matrices to be shown first by strict protocol
Because the comparison matrix replaces the need for a presentation entirely
Because Lesson 15's matrix is the only part of the course scored by review boards
Because establishing consistent criteria (volume, latency tolerance, failure risk) up front lets every individual design choice that follows be judged against criteria the panel already has in view
questions.explain: Opening with the matrix mirrors Lesson 17's presentation structure -- it sets up shared criteria so later decisions can be evaluated against something the panel has already seen, rather than appearing arbitrary.

questions.q: How does Priya answer Panelist 1's 'why isn't everything behind one middleware hub' objection?
options: By insisting the hub is unconditionally superior to point-to-point in every case
By refusing to answer since the panel's question is out of scope

By conceding point-to-point's simplicity for a single connection, then pointing at the maintenance-cost tradeoff that justifies the hub for new work while migrating the highest-maintenance existing connection
By claiming Doverfield has no point-to-point connections at all
questions.explain: This follows Lesson 18's Objection 1 pattern exactly: partial concession followed by the specific tradeoff that justifies the actual design decision.

questions.q: How does Priya answer Panelist 2's question about CDC being used for some objects but not others?
options: By naming the actual criterion behind the split -- freshness and delete-sensitivity needs per object -- and connecting it to Lesson 15's matrix rather than claiming a blanket rule
By admitting the split was arbitrary and apologizing for it
By claiming CDC is always the better choice and the incremental-extract objects should be migrated immediately
By refusing to discuss the data warehouse sync during the review
questions.explain: She connects the seemingly inconsistent choice back to a previously established criterion (failure-risk and freshness profile per object), showing the split is deliberate rather than arbitrary.

questions.q: What does Priya's answer to Panelist 3 demonstrate, per Lesson 18's Objection 4 pattern?
options: Confident assertion that the design works, with no supporting evidence given
An honest description of an actual sandbox test that was run before go-live, specifying what the test checked, rather than just asserting confidence
A refusal to discuss whether the resilience design was tested
A claim that testing resilience designs is unnecessary for integration architecture
questions.explain: Objection 4's pattern specifically calls for real evidence of testing (or an honest admission if testing hasn't happened), not just confident assertion -- Priya describes the actual sandbox test performed.

questions.q: Per this lesson, what does a review panel score beyond whether the final technical answer was correct?
options: Only the visual quality of the presentation slides
The total number of objections the candidate can correctly predict in advance
Whether the candidate used the exact same wording as the course material
How the candidate reasoned and defended each answer -- conceding valid points, connecting answers back to established criteria, and having actual evidence rather than just confidence
questions.explain: A candidate who answers correctly but argues defensively or invents justifications on the spot scores worse than one who reasons visibly and honestly, even if their final answers require more humility.
